steps: Review the privacy labels on your report suite and record each labelled variable, with its matching schema field, in a label inventory.
Mark the matching schema fields as identities, and apply the data usage labels by hand, since Experience Platform does not copy them from Adobe Analytics.
Agree with your privacy team how privacy requests are handled for the Analytics dataset, and record the process in a short runbook.
Check the labels and identities against the inventory with your privacy owner before the dataset is enabled for Profile.
deliverables: Privacy request runbook for the Analytics dataset
Signed-off review before Profile is enabled
asks: A privacy or data governance owner who can sign off the labels
Access to the report suite's privacy settings and the Experience Platform schema
risk: A field reaching profiles without its label: we label by hand from the inventory and get sign-off before the dataset is enabled for Profile.
outcome: Your Analytics data enters profiles with its identities marked and its data usage labels in place, so your data usage policies apply to it.

steps: Agree with your marketing and analytics teams which Real-Time CDP audiences to share, and what each one should answer in reporting.
Connect the Experience Cloud Audiences destination and activate the agreed audiences to Audience Manager and Adobe Analytics.
Check that each audience arrives in Audience Manager and shows in Analytics, and record the results in a short audience register.
Walk your analysts through the shared audiences in Analytics, so they know what each one contains and where it came from.
asks: Decisions from your marketing and analytics teams on which audiences to share
Admin access to Real-Time CDP destinations and to Audience Manager
risk: Sharing audiences with sensitive attributes: we agree each audience with your team and keep sensitive attributes out unless you approve them.
outcome: Your analysts see the agreed Real-Time CDP audiences in Adobe Analytics, beside the rest of your site data.

steps: Submit the A4T provisioning request together with your admin, and set up user access to the report suite for the people who run activities.
Enable Analytics in the datastream, or bring the page libraries to the releases Adobe requires, on a test environment first.
Set Adobe Analytics as the reporting source in Target for the agreed activities, and record the settings in a configuration note.
Run a test activity and check that Target and Analytics hits share the same ID, before any live activity reports through A4T.
deliverables: A4T provisioned and user access set
asks: An admin who can submit the provisioning request and grant report suite access
A test environment and a low-risk page for the first activity
risk: Target and Analytics hits that do not share the same ID: we test a trial activity end to end before any live activity reports through A4T.
outcome: Adobe Analytics is the reporting source for your Target activities, so every Analytics metric and segment is available on each activity's report.

steps: Agree with your testing and analytics teams the success metrics and segments each activity reports on, and record them in a readout plan.
Build the test readout in Analysis Workspace with the Analytics for Target panel, showing each experience's lift and confidence on the agreed metrics.
Explain to both teams how A4T counts entrants, with a worked example on one of your activities, so everyone reads results the same way.
Save the readout as a shared project that each new activity starts from, so every test is read with the same layout and metrics.
deliverables: Readout plan with agreed metrics and segments
Walkthrough on how entrants are counted
asks: Your testing and analytics leads, to agree success metrics and segments
A recent or live Target activity to build the first readout on
risk: The two teams reading the same test differently: we agree the metrics up front and walk both through how entrants are counted.
outcome: Your teams read each Target activity's lift and confidence in one agreed Analysis Workspace readout, on the metrics you chose.

steps: Agree the product pages and purchase events to track, and implement the product variables Recommendations needs in Adobe Analytics.
Create the Analytics classifications feed in Target and map its columns to the Recommendations fields, recorded in a mapping sheet.
Set up a test criteria that uses Analytics as its behavioral data source, drawing on view-based and purchase-based data.
Check the test criteria's recommendations against known product views and purchases on a test page, and record the results before any live activity.
deliverables: Classifications feed and field mapping sheet
asks: Your product catalog owner, to confirm the product IDs used on the site
Access to the report suite and to Target Recommendations
risk: Product IDs that differ between the site and the feed: we agree one ID in the mapping sheet and test the criteria before launch.
outcome: Your Target Recommendations activities can use the view-based and purchase-based behavioral data you already collect in Adobe Analytics.

steps: Pass your report suite ID when the PDF viewer is created on your pages, in the AdobeDC.View instance, and agree which documents to measure.
Create the processing rules that map the PDF events and their attributes to Analytics variables, recorded in a variable map.
Build the report on documents opened, pages read, downloads and searches in Analysis Workspace, and check it against a set of test views.
deliverables: PDF events flowing into your report suite
asks: Access to the page code that loads the PDF viewer
Admin access to the report suite to create processing rules
risk: PDF events landing in variables already in use: we agree free variables in the map first and test with known document views.
outcome: Your reports show which documents people open, read, download and search, beside your other site data.

steps: Agree with your team leads which teams send for signature from Acrobat and which use Acrobat Sign Solutions, by type of document.
Write the short guide on requesting e-signatures, tracking agreements and saving agreements as templates in Acrobat, with your own documents as examples.
Train each team with hands-on exercises, sending a test document through Request e-signatures and tracking it to completion.
Collect questions after the first weeks of use and update the guide, so it answers what your teams actually ask.
asks: Team leads who can decide how each team sends documents for signature
Time from each team for a training session
risk: Teams sending the same kind of document in different ways: we agree one route per document type and build it into the guide and training.
outcome: Your staff send, track and reuse agreements from Acrobat in one agreed way, with a guide to turn to.

steps: Inventory the PDF forms to convert with your form owners, recording each form's signers, required fields and validations.
Name each form's fields in Acrobat with Acrobat Sign's text tag syntax, so signer roles, required fields and validations carry over.
Upload the prepared forms to the Acrobat Sign Document Library as templates, and check that each field converted as planned.
Send each template for a test signature with your form owner, and record their sign-off in the form inventory.
deliverables: Form inventory with signers and fields
Prepared PDF forms with tagged fields
asks: The PDF forms to convert, in their current versions
A form owner for each form who can approve the test signature
risk: A field that loses its role or validation on upload: we test each template with a signature before your teams use it.
outcome: Your forms are reusable Acrobat Sign library templates, with signer roles, required fields and validations already in place.

steps: Agree the agreement types, the data fields each needs and the source system with your sales and legal teams, recorded in a field map.
Prepare the Word templates and place the signature fields as Acrobat Sign text tags with the Adobe Document Generation Tagger.
Build the flow that fills each template with your data through the Document Generation API and sends the result through the Acrobat Sign API.
Test the flow with sample records for each agreement type, checking the merged data and the signature fields, and get your legal team's sign-off.
deliverables: Field map for each agreement type
asks: Your current agreement documents and the approved wording for each
Access to the system that holds the data, and a technical contact
risk: Wrong data merged into a legal document: we test each template with sample records and get your legal team's sign-off before go-live.
outcome: Agreements are generated from your data and sent for signature automatically, without retyping or placing fields by hand.

steps: Create the PDF Embed API client ID for your site domains, and set the PDF Viewer component's context-aware configuration with your administrator.
Add the PDF Viewer component to the agreed page templates, deployed through Cloud Manager with the rest of the site's code.
Agree with your authors the viewer type and the tools visitors get, such as download, print or annotate, and record them in an authoring note.
deliverables: PDF Embed API client ID and configuration
PDF Viewer component on page templates
asks: An AEM administrator who can set the context-aware configuration
The list of site domains where PDFs will be shown
risk: A viewer that will not load on a site domain left off the PDF Embed API client ID: we list every domain first and test each one.
outcome: PDFs from your asset library open inside your pages, in the viewer and with the tools your authors chose.

steps: Decide with your admins which groups keep the Adobe Express integration on, and turn off the Express services in the product profile for the rest.
Make your brand kits and templates available to the groups that keep it, with your brand team approving what is shared.
Show each team how to stylize a PDF, edit its images and bring the file back into Acrobat, in short hands-on sessions.
asks: An administrator who manages your Acrobat product profiles
Your brand team's approved brand kits and templates
risk: Off-brand documents from teams using Express freely: we share only approved brand kits and templates, and switch it off where it is not needed.
outcome: Your chosen teams restyle PDFs and edit their images from inside Acrobat, starting from your approved brand kits and templates.

steps: Agree the document steps to automate with your Workfront admins, such as generating a PDF from Workfront data or combining documents on a task.
Create the PDF Services connection in Workfront Fusion, with its credentials held under an account your team owns.
Build each agreed scenario, such as converting and combining documents or reading data from a PDF into custom form fields, saving results to the work.
Test each scenario with sample documents, check the output, and hand over a runbook for each one with what to do when a run fails.
deliverables: PDF Services connection in Workfront Fusion
asks: A Workfront admin who can approve the scenarios and the custom form fields
Sample documents for each scenario, including the awkward ones
risk: A scenario that fails quietly on an unusual document: we test with your hardest samples and set out in each runbook what to do when a run fails.
outcome: Your Workfront processes create, convert, combine and read PDF files on their own, with results saved to the work they belong to.

steps: List the Foundation Components forms that need signing with your form owners, such as forms from the Automated Forms Conversion service.
Enable Acrobat Sign on each form and set the signers, their order and the signer authentication agreed with your team.
Place the Adobe Sign fields in each form with the Adobe Sign Block component, and set the document each signer receives.
Test each form end to end with test signers, checking the signing order and that the signed copy and status return to your process.
deliverables: Signing setup for each agreed form
asks: A form owner for each form who decides the signers and their order
Your rules on how each signer must prove who they are
risk: A signer receiving the wrong document or signing out of order: we test each form with test signers before it goes live.
outcome: People sign your forms electronically in the order you set, and the signed copy and its status return to your process.

steps: Agree with your CRM and marketing admins whether agreements sync under lead, contact or account, based on how your teams use them.
Enable sync for the Agreement custom object under the agreed parent in Marketo Engage, and expose the agreement fields to triggers.
Check a sample of synced agreement records against your CRM, field by field, and record the results in a reconciliation note.
deliverables: Agreement object synced in Marketo Engage
asks: Admin access to Marketo Engage and to your CRM
A decision on whether agreements belong under lead, contact or account
risk: Agreements attached to the wrong records: we agree the parent object first and reconcile a sample against your CRM before triggers use the data.
outcome: Your agreement records arrive in Marketo Engage from your CRM, with their fields ready for campaign triggers.

steps: Agree the reminder period, the wording and the sender with your team, and whether signers also hear when an agreement is on its way.
Build the Marketo Engage program with tokens that carry the agreement name and signing link, and write the reminder email.
Set up the smart campaign that sends the reminder when an agreement stays unsigned for the agreed period, with its Smart List and flow.
Test the campaign with test agreements and test people, checking the tokens, the link and the timing before it goes live.
asks: The reminder period and approved wording for the reminder email
Test agreements in your CRM that we can leave unsigned
risk: A reminder sent for an agreement that is already signed: we test the campaign's filters with test agreements in each state before launch.
outcome: Signers get a reminder with their signing link when an agreement stays unsigned, without anyone chasing them by hand.

steps: Agree which Workfront tasks, issues or projects need a signature, and which Workfront fields hold the signers, recorded in a mapping sheet.
Build the Workfront Fusion scenario with the Acrobat Sign modules to upload the document and create the agreement with the mapped signers.
Set the point in your Workfront process that starts the scenario, so documents go for signature without anyone sending them by hand.
Test the scenario with sample work items and test signers, and hand over a runbook covering failed runs and changed signers.
asks: A Workfront admin who can add or confirm the signer fields
Sample documents and test signers for each kind of work item
risk: A document sent to the wrong signer: we take signers only from agreed Workfront fields and test each kind of work item before go-live.
outcome: Documents on your Workfront tasks, issues and projects go to Acrobat Sign for signature automatically, to the right signers.

steps: Agree with your Workfront admins what each agreement event means for the task: the status after it is signed, declined or expired.
Build the Workfront Fusion scenario with the trigger module that starts on the selected agreement events, and map each event to its update.
Update the task, its status and its documents on each event, attaching the signed copy to the work it belongs to.
Test each event with test agreements, signed, declined and left to expire, and record the results in the scenario runbook.
asks: The Workfront statuses your teams use for signed, declined and expired work
A Workfront admin to approve the status changes
risk: A task left showing the wrong status after a decline or expiry: we test every event type before go-live and document each in the runbook.
outcome: Your Workfront tasks show each agreement's outcome as it happens, with the signed copy attached where your team works.

steps: Agree the ad networks and ad accounts to bring in with your media team, from Google Ads, Meta, Pinterest, Snapchat or TikTok.
Authorize the Experience Platform advertising source for each agreed account once your ad admins approve access in that network.
Add the paid media datasets the sources create to your Customer Journey Analytics connection and data view as summary data.
Compare a recent day's spend and clicks in each network with the summary data, and record the results in a source log.
deliverables: Authorized advertising sources for each agreed account
Paid media datasets in the CJA connection
asks: Ad admins in each network who can approve access to the agreed accounts
The list of ad accounts and networks to include
risk: A source held up waiting for an ad admin's approval: we agree the admins and accounts in the first week and track each approval.
outcome: Your paid media data from the agreed networks sits in Customer Journey Analytics beside your web data, as summary data.

steps: Agree the IDs in your landing page URLs with your media team, so each network's campaign, ad group and ad IDs are present.
Build the derived fields that read the network and campaign IDs from landing page URLs, and set up the summary data groups.
Build the Workspace reports for web ROAS, cost per web order and the gap between what the networks report and what your site records.
Check the joins on a recent week against each network's own figures, and walk your media and analytics teams through the reports.
deliverables: Derived fields for network and campaign IDs
Web ROAS and cost per web order reports
asks: Your media team's URL tagging rules for each network
Agreement on which site events count as a web order
risk: Landing page URLs missing their campaign IDs, so spend cannot join conversions: we audit the tagging first and list the campaigns to fix.
outcome: Your team reads web ROAS and cost per web order by network and campaign, and sees where network and site figures differ.

steps: Connect each agreed ad destination with the ad account your team permits, and record the account and its owner in a destination log.
Map each destination's supported identities and apply its normalization and hashing rules, agreed with your privacy team before any data leaves.
Activate a first audience to each destination, and review the platform's reported match rates where available, recording them in the log.
deliverables: First audience activated to each destination
asks: Ad account access in each platform from your media team
Your privacy team's approval of the identities to send
risk: Identities sent without the right hashing, or poor matches: we agree the identity rules with your privacy team and test with one audience first.
outcome: Your Real-Time CDP audiences reach the agreed ad platforms with the right identities, and you see each platform's reported match rate where available.

steps: Agree the marketers who need assets in Journey Optimizer, and add them to the Assets Cloud Services product profiles.
Select the Assets as a Cloud Service repository in Journey Optimizer, so marketers pick assets from it in the Email Designer.
Set up the campaign asset folders with your DAM owner, and test that a marketer can place an asset in a test email.
deliverables: Marketers added to Assets product profiles
asks: The list of marketers who build emails in Journey Optimizer
Your DAM owner, to agree the campaign folder structure
risk: Marketers picking unapproved or outdated images: we agree the campaign folders with your DAM owner and show marketers where approved assets sit.
outcome: Your marketers pick images from your AEM Assets repository while building emails in Journey Optimizer, from agreed campaign folders.

steps: Agree the renditions and image parameters each channel needs with your marketing and DAM teams, recorded in a rendition sheet.
Set up the approved renditions and image parameters in Dynamic Media, so marketers pick them in the asset selector with Content Advisor.
Place a rendition in a test message, change the source asset in AEM, and check that the message picks up the latest version.
Show your marketers how to choose renditions in the asset selector, with a short guide on which one suits each channel.
asks: Your DAM owner, to approve the renditions and image parameters
The channels and image sizes your messages use today
risk: Marketers using the wrong size or crop for a channel: we agree the renditions in the sheet and cover the choice in the guide.
outcome: Journey content uses approved renditions that stay current when assets change in AEM, without marketers replacing images by hand.

steps: List your recurring DAM tasks with your DAM team, such as a new brand or campaign folder, channel renditions and metadata completeness checks.
Write a Skill for each agreed task, each with a confirmation step before any change, using the Onboarding skills or AEM where Content Discovery cannot write.
Test each Skill on a test folder with your DAM team, covering everyday requests and edge cases, and record the results.
Hand over each Skill with a short guide on when to use it and what it changes, and train your DAM team on it.
asks: Your DAM team's list of recurring tasks and how they do them today
A test area in AEM Assets where Skills can run safely
risk: A Skill changing assets nobody intended: every Skill asks for confirmation before a change, and each is tested on a test folder first.
outcome: Your DAM team runs its recurring folder, rendition and metadata tasks through Coworker Chat, with a confirmation before each change.

steps: Agree with each team the custom metadata properties they search by, such as campaign, brand or license, and record them in a property list.
Index the agreed custom metadata properties in AEM Assets, and check the fields are filled on the assets teams search most.
Test discovery prompts with each team in Coworker Chat, record which ones find the right assets, and fix the metadata gaps the tests show.
asks: A contact from each team that searches the DAM
Your DAM owner's approval of the property list
risk: Prompts that miss assets because their metadata is empty: we check the fields are filled and test prompts with each team before handover.
outcome: Your teams find assets in Coworker Chat by the campaign, brand or license fields they already use.

steps: Agree with your authors where they write, in Word, Google Docs or the Universal Editor, and whether assets go in as copies or references.
Set up the AEM Assets Sidekick plugin or the custom asset picker in the Universal Editor, with the agreed repositories and filters.
Test the picker with authors on sample pages, place an asset in each mode, publish, and check the asset appears on the page.
Write a one-page authoring guide on picking assets, and train your authors on it with their own pages.
deliverables: Configured asset picker for your authors
asks: Your authoring lead, to decide between copies and references
Access to the AEM Assets repositories authors will use
risk: Authors inserting copies that drift from the approved asset: we agree copy or reference mode up front and show authors which to use.
outcome: Your authors place assets from AEM Assets into pages as they write, from the agreed repositories and filters.

steps: Agree the image sizes, crops, formats and quality settings for each block with your design team, recorded in an image sheet.
Update the block code, and the importer where pages are imported, to turn AEM Assets delivery URLs into responsive image markup.
Place approved assets by reference on sample pages, including video and PDF links, and check each renders as planned on mobile and desktop.
Run Lighthouse on the sample pages after the change, and fix anything that lowers the score before release.
deliverables: Updated block code for responsive images
asks: Your design team's image sizes and crops for each block
Access to the GitHub repository for the site's code
risk: Images that render static or slow the pages: we test the sample pages on mobile and desktop and run Lighthouse on each change.
outcome: Your Edge Delivery pages show approved assets as responsive images, sized and formatted for each screen from one source.

steps: Agree the workflows and bulk actions that read from and write to AEM Assets, and the source and destination folders, with your DAM owner.
Set AEM Assets as the cloud source on each input node and as the destination on each output node.
Set up access for the users and folders involved, and record it in an access sheet your DAM owner signs off.
Test a run end to end on the Author tier, from source files to finished files, and fix any access gaps it shows.
deliverables: Access sheet for users and folders
asks: Your DAM owner, to agree source and destination folders
The workflows and bulk actions your production team runs
risk: A run that fails on folder access part way through: we set access from a signed-off sheet and test end to end before handover.
outcome: Your production workflows read source files from AEM Assets and write finished files back to the folders you agreed.

steps: Agree with your DAM owner where generated variants land in AEM Assets, and how they are named and tagged.
Agree how each variant traces back to its hero asset and the workflow that made it, recorded in a rules sheet.
Apply the rules to the output nodes of each workflow, run a test, and check the variants against the rules sheet.
Hand the rules sheet to your production team, with examples of correctly named and tagged variants from the test run.
deliverables: Folder, naming and tagging rules sheet
Output nodes set to the rules
asks: Your DAM owner, to agree folders, names and tags
Examples of hero assets and the variants made from them
risk: Generated variants piling up untraceable in the DAM: we agree the rules first and test them on a run before production use.
outcome: Every generated variant lands in an agreed folder with a name and tags that trace it back to its hero asset.

steps: Check that AEM Assets and GenStudio for Performance Marketing sit in the same organization, and enable Content Hub in Cloud Manager where it is off.
Add your GenStudio users, or a user group, to the AEM Assets Content Hub product profile in the Admin Console.
Check that the Location list in GenStudio Content shows the repository, and that a creator can open an approved asset from it.
deliverables: Content Hub enabled for your AEM Assets
GenStudio users in the Content Hub product profile
asks: An Admin Console administrator for your organization
The list of GenStudio users, or the group to add
risk: The two products sitting in different organizations, so the repository never appears: we check the organization first, before any other setup.
outcome: Your creators see your approved Content Hub assets in GenStudio's Content library, ready to start new ads and emails.

steps: Set up the approval fields in your AEM Assets metadata schema, agreed with your DAM owner, and record who may approve assets.
Approve the assets your creators need for Content Hub with your brand team, and check expiry dates on licensed assets before approval.
Configure Content Hub's filters, asset details and search around the fields your creators look for, such as campaign or product.
Test with your creators in GenStudio that they find the approved assets they need, and adjust the filters from their feedback.
deliverables: Approval fields in the metadata schema
Approved asset set in Content Hub
Configured filters, asset details and search
asks: Your brand team, to approve the assets creators may use
License terms and expiry dates for your licensed assets
risk: Expired licensed assets reaching new ads: we check expiry dates before approval and record them in each asset's metadata.
outcome: Your creators find approved, in-date assets in GenStudio, through filters and search set up around how they work.

steps: Check with your admins that your Marketo subscription is on Adobe IMS, which the Email Designer needs, and that Dynamic Media with OpenAPI is on.
Generate the service credential certificate, and link the Delivery tier repository in Marketo Admin.
Add your email authors to the Assets product profiles, and test that an author can pick a DAM image in the Email Designer.
Record the certificate's expiry date in a handover note, with a reminder and the steps to renew it, owned by your admin.
deliverables: Linked Delivery tier repository in Marketo
Email authors in the Assets product profiles
Handover note with certificate renewal steps
asks: Admins for Marketo Engage and AEM Assets who can make the link
The list of email authors who need DAM images
risk: An expired certificate breaking the link without warning: we record the expiry date, set a reminder and hand your admin the renewal steps.
outcome: Your email authors pick DAM images in the Email Designer, and changes made in AEM reach your live emails.

steps: Inventory your email templates and visual fragments with your email team, listing the images stored in Marketo that each one uses.
Set AEM Assets as the image source on each template and visual fragment, and swap the Marketo-stored images for DAM-linked ones.
Agree with your DAM owner who may change or delete images used in live emails, since a deleted image breaks them.
Send test emails from each template, check every image loads from the DAM, and record the results in the inventory.
deliverables: Templates and fragments on DAM-linked images
Rules for changing images in live emails
asks: Your email team, to list the templates and fragments in use
Your DAM owner, to agree who may change live images
risk: A deleted DAM image breaking live emails: we agree who may change or delete those images and tag them so they are easy to spot.
outcome: Your email templates draw their images from AEM Assets, so an approved change in AEM reaches your live emails.

steps: Inventory the linked folders, documents and use cases on your legacy or enhanced connector with your Workfront and DAM owners.
Agree the critical use cases with your teams, and write a test for each, with an expected result your owners sign off.
Move the existing linked folders and documents to the native integration, and run every critical use case test on it.
Uninstall the old connector once the tests pass, since it cannot run alongside the native one, following an agreed cutover plan.
deliverables: Connector inventory and critical use case list
Linked folders and documents on the native integration
asks: Workfront and DAM owners who can name the critical use cases
An agreed window for the cutover, when teams pause linked work
risk: A use case that only worked on the old connector: we test every critical use case on the native integration before uninstalling it.
outcome: Your Workfront and AEM Assets work runs on the native integration, with your linked folders and documents moved across.

steps: Agree the gaps the native integration leaves with your Workfront and DAM teams, such as metadata updates or asset imports from a URL.
Set up the server-to-server credentials with write access, under an account your admins own, and record where they are kept.
Build each agreed Workfront Fusion scenario with the AEM Assets connector, including scenarios that start when an asset changes in AEM.
Test each scenario on a test folder with sample assets, and hand over a runbook on what it does and what to do when a run fails.
asks: An admin who can create the server-to-server credentials with write access
A test folder in AEM Assets with sample assets
risk: A scenario with write access changing the wrong assets: we build and test each one on a test folder before it touches live folders.
outcome: Your Workfront Fusion scenarios create, update and move assets in AEM Assets where the native integration stops short.

steps: Connect the agreed record types in Workfront Planning, such as campaigns, to AEM Assets, and choose the lookup fields each one shows.
Agree with your planning and DAM teams how they link images, folders and Content Fragments to records, recorded in a short guide.
Link a sample campaign's assets with your team, check the lookup fields show as planned, and adjust the guide from what they find.
deliverables: Record types connected to AEM Assets
asks: Your planning lead, to name the record types to connect
A sample campaign whose assets we can link together
risk: Teams linking assets in different ways, so records are hard to read: we agree one approach in the guide and test it on a sample campaign.
outcome: Your campaign records in Workfront Planning link to their images, folders and Content Fragments in AEM Assets.

steps: Agree with your Workfront and DAM owners which projects send documents to AEM Assets, and which Workfront fields map to asset metadata.
Connect Workfront to your Experience Manager Assets repository, and set up the field to metadata mapping, recorded in a mapping sheet.
In Workfront's classic Documents area, set up the linked folder trees and the project template workflows that create folders and publish assets.
Test with a sample project end to end, from template to published asset, and check the metadata arrives as mapped.
deliverables: Linked folder trees and template workflows
asks: Workfront and DAM owners who can agree the field mapping
The project templates your teams use most
risk: Teams working in the new Documents area, where the template workflows are not available: we agree which area each team uses before setup.
outcome: Finished documents move from your Workfront projects into AEM Assets with their mapped metadata, into folders created for each project.

steps: Add the Customheaderlibs and Customfooterlibs client libraries to your site's page components, deployed through the Cloud Manager pipeline.
Allow the Adaptive Forms Container in the agreed page templates, so authors can create a form inside a page or Experience Fragment.
Build or embed the first agreed forms on pages and Experience Fragments, using the Adaptive Forms Embed component for existing forms.
Test each form in the stage environment, from page load to submission, and walk your authors through adding a form.
deliverables: Client libraries on your page components
First forms live on agreed pages
asks: The first forms to build or embed, with their owners
Access to the site's code repository and Cloud Manager pipeline
risk: A form that works on its own but breaks inside a page: we test each one in stage, on the pages it will live on.
outcome: Your authors create and place adaptive forms inside your AEM Sites pages and Experience Fragments, on templates that allow them.

steps: Agree the forms the portal lists and the pages it sits on with your forms owners, and agree how people sign in to the site.
Build the portal pages with the Search & Lister, Drafts & Submissions and Link components, styled to match your site.
Connect your Azure Storage through the Unified Storage Connector, with an account and access that your team owns and approves.
Test as a signed-in user: start a form, save a draft, resume it and submit, then check the submission shows in the portal.
deliverables: Unified Storage Connector linked to your Azure Storage
asks: Your Azure Storage account details and an administrator to connect it
Your site sign-in setup and a test account
risk: Only signed-in people can resume drafts and see submissions: we agree sign-in with you first and make that clear on the portal pages.
outcome: Signed-in visitors find your forms, resume their saved drafts and see their submissions on your site's portal pages.

steps: Review your site theme and current form styles with your design team, and agree the form styles that follow the site.
Embed the Adaptive Forms theme in your AEM Sites theme, so one build and one front-end pipeline deployment style both.
Deploy to stage and check sample pages with embedded forms on mobile and desktop, with your design team signing off.
deliverables: One combined site and forms theme
asks: Your design team, to agree form styles and sign off
Access to the site's theme code and front-end pipeline
risk: Form styles clashing with page styles: we agree the styles first and review sample pages in stage before release.
outcome: Your site pages and the forms on them share one theme, built and deployed together.

steps: Prepare the guidelines document and the templates and themes on your author instance that Coworker picks from, agreed with your forms team.
Pilot Coworker creating and updating adaptive forms from your briefs, screenshots or PDFs, on a sample of agreed forms.
Write the prompts your team will reuse, refined from what worked in the pilot, and collect them in a prompt guide.
Set the review step before any form is published, with a named reviewer who checks the form through the link Coworker returns.
deliverables: Templates and themes on the author instance
asks: Sample briefs, screenshots or PDFs of forms to build in the pilot
A reviewer who approves forms before they are published
risk: A generated form published with a wrong field or rule: every form passes a named reviewer in the editor before it is published.
outcome: Your forms team describes a form or change in plain words, and Coworker builds it in your AEM environment for review.

steps: Agree with your forms team which submit connectors, Form Data Model services and custom functions their forms need, recorded in a list.
Configure each one in AEM first, since Coworker only uses connectors and services that already exist there.
Test rule and submission prompts with your team in Coworker Chat, and record which prompts set the right connector and rules.
deliverables: Configured submit connectors and Form Data Model services
asks: Your forms team's list of where submissions must go
Access to the back-end systems the connectors use
risk: Prompts asking for a connector that does not exist yet: we configure every agreed one first and test the prompts against them.
outcome: Coworker sets your forms' rules and submissions using connectors and services already configured in AEM.

steps: Collect your existing PDF and XDP forms with their owners, and store the agreed ones in the AEM DAM in a dedicated folder.
Import each form into an adaptive form with Coworker, and record each converted form in a tracking sheet.
Review each form's fields, rules and layout in the editor with its owner, fix any gaps, and record the sign-off.
deliverables: Source forms stored in the AEM DAM
asks: Your existing PDF and XDP forms in their current versions
A form owner for each form to review the result
risk: A converted form missing a field or rule: every form is reviewed in the editor with its owner before it is used.
outcome: Your existing PDF and XDP forms become reviewed adaptive forms, signed off by their owners and ready to publish.

steps: Add the Adaptive Forms Block to your Edge Delivery repository, or start from the AEM Forms boilerplate for a new site, as agreed with your team.
Connect AEM Code Sync to the repository and link the AEM author, so forms authored there render on your pages.
Create the first agreed forms from the Edge Delivery template in the Universal Editor, with your authors working beside us.
Publish the forms, test each one from page load to submission, and run Lighthouse on the pages that carry them.
deliverables: Adaptive Forms Block in your repository
AEM Code Sync and author connection
asks: Admin access to your Edge Delivery GitHub repository
The first forms to build, with an owner for each
risk: A form that slows the page it sits on: we run Lighthouse on each page with a form and test each change.
outcome: Your authors create forms in the Universal Editor that render on your Edge Delivery pages through the Adaptive Forms Block.

steps: Agree with your team which forms submit to AEM Publish, and which workflows, Form Data Model or submit actions process each one.
Set the publish URL in the form block for each agreed form, and record it in a submission map.
Set the Referrer Filter and the Dispatcher CORS rules for each site domain, and list each domain's settings in the map.
Test a submission from each domain and form, and check it reaches AEM Publish and its workflow or submit action runs.
deliverables: Submission map by form and domain
Publish URL, Referrer Filter and CORS settings
asks: The list of site domains that will submit forms
An AEM administrator who can change the Referrer Filter and Dispatcher rules
risk: Submissions blocked from a domain missing from the rules: we list every domain in the map and test a submission from each one.
outcome: Form submissions from your Edge Delivery pages reach AEM Publish, where your workflows and submit actions process them.
